title: Deepest-path variables match a term's free literals
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ Boolean variables and $\rho$ a restriction, and let $t$ be the first term of $f$, in list order, that is not killed by $\rho$. Suppose the literals of $t$ are pairwise distinct and no two of them share a variable, and write $l_{i_0}, l_{i_1}, \ldots$ for the subsequence of literals of $t$ whose variables are free under $\rho$, taken in their order of occurrence in $t$. Then for every index $k$ smaller than both the number of these free literals and the length of the deepest root-to-leaf path of the canonical decision tree of $f$ under $\rho$, the variable queried at the $k$-th step of that path equals the variable of the $k$-th free literal $l_{i_k}$.
hypotheses_covered: t is the first term of f not killed by ρ
no two literals of t share a variable
flis is the free literals of t (variable free under ρ), in term order
k below the number of free literals
k below the length of the deepest path
replaced:
When $f.\mathrm{find?}$ returns an alive clause $t$ and $\mathrm{flis}$ is the
filtered (zipIdx) list of $t$'s free literals under $\rho$, the variable at
position $k$ of $(\mathrm{canonicalDTree}\,f\,\rho).\mathrm{deepPath}$ equals the
variable of the $k$-th free literal, since the canonical tree branches on the
free literals of $t$ in clause order.
